statement: You are given two integer arrays a and b of the same length and an integer count. A sum combination is a[i] + b[j] for one index i of a and one index j of b, and each pair of indices (i, j) may be used at most once.
Return the count largest sum combinations, in non-increasing order.

Rather than forming all a.length × b.length sums, sort both arrays in descending order and start a max-heap with the pair (0, 0), which gives the largest sum. Each time you pop a pair (i, j), record its sum and push (i + 1, j) and (i, j + 1) if they have not been pushed before.

examples.explanation: The largest sum is 4 + 6 = 10. Next come 4 + 5 = 9 and 3 + 6 = 9, then 8, which both 3 + 5 and 2 + 6 reach; only one of them is needed to make up four sums.
8 + 7 = 15, 8 + 4 = 12, 8 + 3 = 11, 4 + 7 = 11, 8 + 2 = 10 and 3 + 7 = 10. Equal sums from different index pairs each count.
All four index pairs give the sum 2. They are different pairs, so three of them can be used.
